# Slice 5.1 — fault-safe user copy + real `SYS_DIAGCTL`

## 1. The PT-walk copy engine

### 1.1 Where it lives: new `kernel/src/mm/uaccess.rs`

**Not** inside `kernel/src/ipc/message.rs`. Three reasons:

- D4 (slice 5.2) needs the identical engine for `do_setgrant`/`do_safecopy`/`do_copy`, which live in `kernel/src/system/`. If the engine sits in `ipc::message` (a private `mod message;` at `kernel/src/ipc/mod.rs:22`), `system` has to reach through `pub(crate) use message::{…}` for byte-level primitives — the wrong direction.
- `kernel/src/mm/mod.rs:32` already owns `phys_to_hhdm`, which is the whole mechanism. HHDM aliasing is an mm concern.
- It keeps `ipc/message.rs` what its name says: a thin `Message`-shaped wrapper (~40 lines) over a generic byte engine.

`kernel/src/mm/mod.rs` gains `pub mod uaccess;` beside `pub mod frame;` (line 22). Per CLAUDE.md line 166, a new kernel module is just `mod foo;` — no `cfg(target_os = "none")` gate.

### 1.2 New free function in `addrspace.rs`

`AddrSpace::walk_pt` (`kernel/src/arch/aarch64/addrspace.rs:129-141`) is unusable here: it is a **method**, it drops `Prot`, and `check_va` (line 289) rejects non-page-aligned VAs. Add the free-function sibling of `map_page_in` (line 173) / `unmap_page_in` (line 201):

```rust
/// Walk the tree rooted at `ttbr0_pa` for the leaf mapping of the page
/// containing `va` (which must be page-aligned), returning `(pa, prot)`.
/// `None` on a walk miss, a misaligned/out-of-range `va`, or `ttbr0_pa == 0`.
///
/// All table access is via HHDM; the target AS need not be the active one —
/// the same contract `map_page_in` / `unmap_page_in` / `walk_leaves` carry.
pub fn walk_pt_in(ttbr0_pa: u64, va: u64) -> Option<(u64, Prot)>
```

It reuses the existing private helpers unchanged — `check_va` (289), `pte_index` (299), `next_table` (331), `table_ref` (316), `PA_MASK` (287), `pte_prot` (271). No visibility changes needed; `Prot` is already `pub` (line 39).

Add the `ttbr0_pa == 0 || ttbr0_pa & (FRAME_SIZE-1) != 0` guard at the top. This is a **genuinely new hazard**: the old code walked the live TTBR0, which was always valid; `walk_pt_in(0, va)` would `table_ref(0)` → `phys_to_hhdm(0)` → read whatever sits at PA 0.

Then re-express the existing method as a one-liner so nothing forks:

```rust
pub fn walk_pt(&self, va: u64) -> Option<u64> {
    walk_pt_in(self.ttbr0_pa, va).map(|(pa, _)| pa)
}
```

`AddrSpace::walk_pt` has **zero call sites** today (only `book/src/memory/overview.md:88` and `docs/plans/phase-3-vm.md:40` reference it), so this is risk-free. Keep it — the docs cite it and the file carries `#![allow(dead_code)]` (line 8).

### 1.3 The engine API

```rust
// kernel/src/mm/uaccess.rs

/// Copy `dst.len()` bytes out of address space `ttbr0_pa` starting at user
/// VA `va`. `Err(EFAULT)` on any unmapped page in the range.
pub fn copy_from_user_as(ttbr0_pa: u64, va: u64, dst: &mut [u8]) -> Result<(), i32>;

/// Copy `src` into address space `ttbr0_pa` at user VA `va`. `Err(EFAULT)`
/// on any unmapped **or non-writable** page in the range; **all-or-nothing**
/// (every page is probed before the first byte is written).
pub fn copy_to_user_as(ttbr0_pa: u64, va: u64, src: &[u8]) -> Result<(), i32>;

/// Verify every page of `[va, va+len)` is mapped in `ttbr0_pa` (and writable
/// when `write`). The pre-pass behind `copy_to_user_as`'s all-or-nothing
/// contract; slice 5.2's `verify_grant` reuses it before a grant copy.
pub fn probe_user_range(ttbr0_pa: u64, va: u64, len: usize, write: bool) -> Result<(), i32>;
```

Taking a raw `ttbr0_pa: u64` (not `&Proc`) matches the `map_page_in`/`unmap_page_in`/`walk_leaves` house style and dodges borrow conflicts — `flush_deliver_msg` holds `&mut Proc` and needs `p.ttbr0_pa`, `p.deliver_msg_vir` and `&p.deliver_msg` simultaneously.

Per-chunk body:

```rust
let (pa, prot) = walk_pt_in(ttbr0_pa, chunk.page_va).ok_or(EFAULT)?;
if write && !prot.writable { return Err(EFAULT); }
// SAFETY: `pa` is a frame this AS's L3 maps; HHDM covers all of [0,4 GiB)
// and QEMU virt RAM is [0x4000_0000, 0x5000_0000) at -m 256M
// (tools/qemu-run.sh:66). Both the HHDM alias and the TTBR0 mapping are
// Normal-WB Inner-Shareable (ATTR_IDX_NORMAL, addrspace.rs:68), and ARMv8
// data caches are PIPT, so the aliases are coherent with no maintenance —
// the same assumption `addrspace::table_mut` already relies on for live
// page tables. Single-threaded, DAIF.I-masked EL1 context: no concurrent
// unmap can race the walk.
unsafe { core::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(...) }
```

**Write-permission check.** Non-negotiable: without it the kernel writes through the HHDM alias into a page EL0 can only read (e.g. stub A's `Prot::RO_CODE` code page at `USER_CODE_VA_A`), which is a protection bypass the old `write_volatile` never had (the MMU would have faulted). `pte_prot` (addrspace.rs:271) already recovers `writable` from the AP bit.

**All-or-nothing on write.** A 104-byte `Message` at offset ≥ 0xF98 in a page straddles two pages. Copy-as-you-go would leave a partial message in a user buffer before returning EFAULT. Probe-first costs one extra 4-level walk of ≤ 2 pages per message — noise next to the copy itself — and makes the EFAULT contract clean. `copy_from_user_as` does not need it (the kernel-side staging buffer is discarded on error), so keep it write-only.

### 1.4 Pure logic that moves to `kernel-shared` (host-tested)

The page-chunking arithmetic is the one piece of this slice with real off-by-one risk, and CLAUDE.md line 170 is explicit that there is no `#[cfg(test)]` under `kernel/src/`. Put it in `kernel-shared/src/message.rs`, immediately below `user_va_ok` (line 64) — that file already owns user-VA geometry (`USER_VA_TOP`, line 52, is imported by `addrspace.rs:33`):

```rust
/// 4 KiB user page granule — the one the kernel's stage-1 walker uses.
pub const USER_PAGE_SIZE: u64 = 4096;

/// One page-bounded slice of a user buffer.
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PageChunk {
    pub page_va: u64,   // page-aligned base of the containing page
    pub offset: usize,  // byte offset within that page
    pub len: usize,     // bytes in this chunk (never crosses the page end)
}

/// Split `[va, va+len)` into per-page chunks, ascending. Empty for `len == 0`.
pub fn page_chunks(va: u64, len: usize) -> PageChunks;   // impl Iterator<Item = PageChunk>
```

Host tests to add next to the existing `user_va_ok` set (`kernel-shared/src/message.rs:77-128`):

1. `size_of::<Message>()` at a page-aligned VA → exactly 1 chunk, `offset == 0`, `len == 104`.
2. 104 bytes at `page_end - 8` → 2 chunks: `(page, 4088, 8)` then `(page+4096, 0, 96)`.
3. 104 bytes at `page_end - 104` → 1 chunk exactly filling the page tail.
4. `len == 0` → zero chunks.
5. A 3-page span → 3 chunks; first/last partial, middle full-page.
6. Property: chunk `len`s sum to `len`; chunks are contiguous; no chunk crosses a page boundary.

Extend the carve-out sentence in `kernel-shared/src/lib.rs:6-9` from "a pure predicate over an ABI shape" to "a pure predicate or geometry helper over an ABI shape". `page_chunks` is integer arithmetic only, so it stays miri-clean (`kernel-shared` is on the CI miri list).

Also add to `kernel-shared` for the diag half (§3): `DIAGCTL_CODE_*`, `DIAG_TEXT_OFF`, `DIAG_TEXT_MAX` in `callnr.rs`, with the usual `const _: () = assert!(…)` guards + host tests.

### 1.5 `kernel/src/ipc/message.rs` rewrite

Both signatures gain the address space:

```rust
pub(crate) fn copy_msg_from_user(ttbr0_pa: u64, va: u64) -> Result<Message, i32>
pub(crate) fn copy_msg_to_user(ttbr0_pa: u64, va: u64, m: &Message) -> Result<(), i32>
```

Body pattern (from-user shown):

```rust
const MSG_BYTES: usize = core::mem::size_of::<Message>();   // 104

if !user_va_ok(va, MSG_BYTES) { return Err(EFAULT); }
let mut buf = [0u8; MSG_BYTES];
uaccess::copy_from_user_as(ttbr0_pa, va, &mut buf)?;
Ok(Message {
    m_source: i32::from_ne_bytes(buf[0..4].try_into().expect("in range")),
    m_type:   i32::from_ne_bytes(buf[4..8].try_into().expect("in range")),
    payload:  buf[8..MSG_BYTES].try_into().expect("in range"),
})
```

Staging through `[u8; 104]` rather than a `*mut u8` view of `Message` means **`ipc/message.rs` ends the slice with zero `unsafe`** (all of it concentrated in `mm/uaccess.rs`), and the `try_into().expect(…)` idiom is exactly the house style already used by `do_setalarm::read_u64` (`kernel/src/system/do_setalarm.rs:62`) and `do_exec::read_i32`. The 8/4/4 offsets are triple-locked: `#[repr(C, align(8))]` (kernel-shared/src/message.rs:33), the host test `message_payload_offset_is_8` (line 92), and the generated C header's `_MINIX_OFFSETOF` static asserts. Cost is one extra 104-byte stack copy per IPC — negligible against a 4-level walk. (The raw-byte-view alternative saves that copy at the price of one `unsafe`; either is defensible, but the staging form is cleaner and matches the `#![forbid]`-adjacent discipline of the rest of the IPC layer.)

`user_va_ok` stays as D5 mandates: it is the only thing that rejects NULL and non-8-aligned VAs before the walk. Note it also now overlaps the walk's `check_va` range check — that's fine, it's the cheap pre-gate.

**Module doc rewrite.** The current doc (`kernel/src/ipc/message.rs:3-22`) is slice-2.5 fiction — "a single hand-rolled TTBR0", "let the hardware fault", "phase 3's VM server replaces this entire helper". Replace it with the D5 contract. This is one of the drive-bys `docs/plans/phase-5-prep.md:232-233` nominates.

## 2. How EFAULT reaches the caller's `x0` — all four sites

The trap ABI: `do_ipc` writes `frame.x[0] = result as u64` at `kernel/src/ipc/mod.rs:118`, and `frame` is `TPIDR_EL1` → the current proc's `p.regs` (parked by `sched::set_tpidr_to`, `kernel/src/proc/sched.rs:259-271`). `el1_return_to_user` restores it.

### Site 1 — `mini_send` (`kernel/src/ipc/send.rs:75`)

Add `let caller_ttbr0 = proc_table[caller_idx].ttbr0_pa;` alongside the existing `caller_endpoint` read at line 55, then `copy_msg_from_user(caller_ttbr0, user_msg_va)`. The existing `Err(e) => return e` already propagates.

Path: `mini_send` → `dispatch` (`ipc/mod.rs:158-212`) → `do_ipc` → `frame.x[0] = -14`.

- Plain `SEND`/`SENDNB`: caller's `x0 = EFAULT` directly.
- `SENDREC`: `do_sendrec` (line 241) returns `send_result` early when `!= OK` (line 256-258), so the RECEIVE half never runs and `MF_REPLY_PEND` is never set. `x0 = EFAULT`. **No change needed.**
- The ordering comment at send.rs:72-74 ("copy precedes deadlock_check deliberately … Keep this ordering") stays valid and now matters more.
- `mini_pf_send` (line 139) and `mini_sched_no_quantum_send` (line 212) construct their messages in-kernel and never touch user memory — untouched.

### Site 2 — kernel-call request copy (`kernel/src/system/mod.rs:122`)

`caller_idx` is already in hand at line 102. Pass `proc_table[caller_idx].ttbr0_pa`. Existing `Err(e) => return e` returns EFAULT as the *IPC-layer* result → `dispatch`'s `SENDREC` arm (`ipc/mod.rs:183-185`) → `do_ipc` → `x0 = -14`. The doc comment at system/mod.rs:89 already contracts this ("Returns the IPC-layer result (`OK`, `EFAULT`, `ECALLDENIED`)").

### Site 3 — kernel-call reply copy (`kernel/src/system/mod.rs:141`)

Same AS, same propagation via `if let Err(e) = … { return e }`. **Add a comment** documenting the semantics this exposes: the kernel call *already ran* and its side effects are committed; the caller sees EFAULT in `x0` and its buffer is untouched (thanks to `copy_to_user_as`'s probe-first all-or-nothing). That is the MINIX shape and matches what the code already did — it just never happened before because the copy couldn't fail without panicking.

Note the `[ksys N]` sampler at line 145-153 is *after* the reply copy, so an EFAULT'd call is not counted. Leave that as-is (matches the early return).

### Site 4 — deferred flush (`kernel/src/ipc/mod.rs:276-286`) — the parked `x0`

```rust
pub fn flush_deliver_msg(p: &mut Proc) {
    if p.misc_flags & MF_DELIVERMSG == 0 {
        return;
    }
    let rc = message::copy_msg_to_user(p.ttbr0_pa, p.deliver_msg_vir, &p.deliver_msg);
    p.misc_flags &= !MF_DELIVERMSG;
    match rc {
        Ok(()) => p.misc_flags &= !MF_MSGFAILED,
        Err(e) => {
            // The receiver asked for delivery into a buffer it does not have
            // mapped (or cannot write). The message is consumed — there is no
            // sender left to re-queue it against — and the failure surfaces in
            // the parked x0 the trap restore path hands back, the same idiom
            // `do_exit::unblock_dependents` uses (do_exit.rs:178).
            p.regs.x[0] = e as i64 as u64;
            p.misc_flags |= MF_MSGFAILED;
            trace_deliver_efault(p.nr, p.deliver_msg_vir);
        }
    }
}
```

Why the parked `x0` is the right slot, verified:

- `MF_MSGFAILED` already exists at `kernel/src/proc/flags.rs:83` (MINIX parity, currently unused; the module carries `#![allow(dead_code)]` at line 6, so no lint churn either way). Setting *and clearing* it keeps it meaningful — "the last delivery to this proc failed" — rather than write-only dead state. Nothing reads it in 5.1; a later signals slice can turn it into `SIGSEGV` (that's what MINIX's `delivermsg()` does).
- **Woken-receiver case** (the normal one): `p` is a different proc from the SVC caller. Its `p.regs.x[0]` currently holds `OK`, written by its own blocking `mini_receive`'s `do_ipc`. Overwriting with EFAULT is exactly right.
- **Same-proc case**: `mini_receive` can return `OK` with `MF_DELIVERMSG` already set (`ipc/receive.rs:78` for a pending notification, `:174` in `walk_caller_q`). Then `do_ipc` writes `frame.x[0] = OK` (line 118), `el1_svc_tail` (line 403) → `schedule_next` → `flush_deliver_msg` on the *same* `p.regs` storage, and the EFAULT write lands last. Correct by construction — `frame` and `p.regs` are the same memory.
- `p.ttbr0_pa` is non-zero by the time flush runs: `switch_ttbr0_with_asid` (sched.rs:320) asserts unconditionally. `copy_to_user_as` still guards defensively.

**Update `kernel/src/proc/sched.rs:310-321`.** The comment currently reads: *"The TTBR0 swap must happen **before** `flush_deliver_msg` — the flush writes via the active TTBR0, so the new proc's AS must already be live."* That constraint is gone. Keep the call order (TTBR0 must be installed before `eret` regardless) but rewrite the comment to say the flush now resolves `p.ttbr0_pa` by HHDM page walk and is address-space-independent, so the ordering is no longer load-bearing.

### New EFAULT trace (immediate path)

`grep` over the whole tree confirms **`EFAULT` is produced by nothing but `ipc/message.rs` today**, so a result-keyed trace in `do_ipc` is unambiguous. Add after line 118, in a helper matching `trace_alarm_fire`'s shape (`ipc/mod.rs:382`):

```rust
if result == EFAULT {
    trace_ipc_efault(caller_nr, call_nr, user_msg_va);
}
// -> "[ipc efault] caller=11 call=1 va=0x900000"
```

Uncounted — it can only fire on a deliberate bad pointer, and if it ever fires spontaneously that is precisely the line you want. `ProcNr`'s `Display` (kernel-shared/src/endpoint.rs:54-58) prints the bare number, matching the existing `[ipc {n}] caller={caller_nr}` format.

And in `flush_deliver_msg`: `"[deliver efault] nr=11 va=0x900000"`.

Both deliberately **uncounted** — the brief is right that `[ipc {n}]` is fragile because of the embedded running counter.

## 3. `SYS_DIAGCTL`

### 3.1 Payload layout

`SYS_DIAGCTL = KERNEL_CALL + 12 = 0x60C` (`kernel-shared/src/callnr.rs:33`) already exists, is blanket-granted to every `SRV_T` priv (`kernel/src/proc/table.rs:485`), and routes to `stubs::do_diagctl` (`kernel/src/system/stubs.rs:37`) via `dispatch_caller_local` (`kernel/src/system/mod.rs:234`). **No new call number, no priv wiring, `NR_KERN_CALLS_PHASE4` stays 18.**

New constants in `kernel-shared/src/callnr.rs`, next to the `VMCTL_*` / `PRIVCTL_SET_USER` subcode block (lines 117-152):

```rust
/// `SYS_DIAGCTL` subcode: print inline text to the kernel console.
/// MINIX 3 (`kernel/system/do_diagctl.c`) passes a `(buf, len)` user pointer
/// here; minix.rs carries the text **inline in the payload** instead, so the
/// debug channel needs no user-copy machinery and can never fault (D2).
pub const DIAGCTL_CODE_DIAG: i32 = 1;
/// Reserved MINIX 3 subcodes, unimplemented (`EINVAL`).
pub const DIAGCTL_CODE_STACKTRACE: i32 = 2;
pub const DIAGCTL_CODE_REGISTER:   i32 = 3;
pub const DIAGCTL_CODE_UNREGISTER: i32 = 4;

/// Offset of the inline text within `Message::payload`.
pub const DIAG_TEXT_OFF: usize = 8;
/// Max inline text bytes per `SYS_DIAGCTL(DIAGCTL_CODE_DIAG)` call.
pub const DIAG_TEXT_MAX: usize = 96 - DIAG_TEXT_OFF;   // 88
```

| payload offset | field | dir |
|---|---|---|
| `0..4` | subcode (i32) — `DIAGCTL_CODE_DIAG` | in |
| `4..8` | text length (i32), `0..=DIAG_TEXT_MAX` | in |
| `8..8+len` | text bytes | in |

88 bytes of text — inside D2's "~90" budget, `DIAG_TEXT_OFF = 8` keeps the text start 8-aligned. Guards: `const _: () = assert!(DIAG_TEXT_OFF + DIAG_TEXT_MAX == 96);` plus a distinctness test over the four subcodes, in `callnr.rs`'s existing `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`.

### 3.2 Kernel handler: new `kernel/src/system/do_diagctl.rs`

Caller-local contract, modeled on `do_setalarm.rs` / `do_getinfo.rs`:

```rust
pub(super) fn do_diagctl(caller: &mut Proc, _caller_priv: &Priv, msg: &mut Message) -> i32
```

1. `mod do_diagctl;` in `kernel/src/system/mod.rs` (alphabetical, between `do_exec` and `do_exit` — line 21-30); swap `SYS_DIAGCTL => stubs::do_diagctl(…)` at line 234 for `do_diagctl::do_diagctl(…)`; drop `enosys_stub!(do_diagctl)` at `stubs.rs:37` and add the "real handler as of slice 5.1" comment beside its siblings (stubs.rs:28-40).
2. Read subcode from `0..4`. `DIAGCTL_CODE_DIAG` → print; 2/3/4 → `EINVAL` with a documented "reserved, deferred" arm; anything else → `EINVAL`.
3. Read `len` from `4..8`. `len < 0 || len as usize > DIAG_TEXT_MAX` → `EINVAL`.
4. Emit, unsampled:

```
[diag <name>] <text>
```

`<name>` is `caller.name` (`kernel/src/proc/proc_struct.rs:129`, `[u8; 16]` NUL-padded) trimmed at the first NUL and UTF-8-validated — the `do_exec` name idiom (`kernel/src/system/do_exec.rs:94-103`). **The name comes from the kernel's proc slot, never the payload, so a server can only ever identify itself** — the same anti-spoof property DS relies on for `m_source`.

5. Sanitize each text byte: pass `0x20..=0x7E`, replace everything else with `.`. This is what keeps a server from injecting `\n`, `\r` or ANSI escapes that would break the `[diag <name>]` line framing and, more importantly, the `grep -aF` boot-marker contract. Write byte-by-byte through `core::fmt::Write` on `Uart::new()` (the house idiom — `use core::fmt::Write; let _ = write!(…)`), with a trailing `writeln!`.
6. Return `OK`. No payload mutation.

**No head-carve / modulo sampling.** DIAGCTL is the debug channel; a sampled debug channel is useless. Rate is caller-controlled. Worth a one-line comment noting a runaway server can flood the console — acceptable for a bring-up channel, same as MINIX.

Also add the new constants to `tools/gen-c-headers/src/callnr_h.rs` in the "kernel-call payload constants" section (lines 156-161) — a new `f.section("SYS_DIAGCTL payload")` with the four subcodes + `DIAG_TEXT_OFF`/`DIAG_TEXT_MAX`, plus whatever snapshot test that file carries. Otherwise the header quietly drifts before the 5.6 ABI freeze.

### 3.3 `server-rt::diag_print` — new `server-rt/src/diag.rs`

`server-rt` is `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` with deps `kernel-shared` + `minix-ipc` — both suffice, **no new dependency**. `ds.rs` is the structural model (a single IPC-trap helper module, coverage-excluded).

```rust
/// Print `s` to the kernel console via `SYS_DIAGCTL(DIAGCTL_CODE_DIAG)`.
/// The kernel prefixes each line with the caller's own (kernel-known) name,
/// so a server needs no identifying prefix of its own.
///
/// Chunking: the inline payload holds `DIAG_TEXT_MAX` (88) bytes, so longer
/// strings are split across successive calls — each chunk becomes its own
/// `[diag <name>]` line. Chunks split on **byte** boundaries, not UTF-8
/// codepoints; the kernel's printable-ASCII sanitizer turns any orphaned
/// continuation byte into '.', so a split can garble a multi-byte character
/// but can never produce invalid output. Keep diag text ASCII.
///
/// Returns `OK`, or the first non-`OK` result (aborting the remaining chunks):
/// the trap's error if the SENDREC failed, else the kernel's reply `m_type`.
pub fn diag_print(s: &str) -> i32 {
    for chunk in s.as_bytes().chunks(DIAG_TEXT_MAX) {
        let rc = diag_send(chunk);
        if rc != OK { return rc; }
    }
    OK
}

fn diag_send(bytes: &[u8]) -> i32 {
    let mut msg = Message { m_source: 0, m_type: SYS_DIAGCTL, payload: [0u8; 96] };
    msg.payload[0..4].copy_from_slice(&DIAGCTL_CODE_DIAG.to_ne_bytes());
    msg.payload[4..8].copy_from_slice(&(bytes.len() as i32).to_ne_bytes());
    msg.payload[DIAG_TEXT_OFF..DIAG_TEXT_OFF + bytes.len()].copy_from_slice(bytes);

    let trap_rc = ipc_sendrec(boot_endpoint(SYSTEM), &mut msg);
    if trap_rc != OK { return trap_rc; }
    msg.m_type
}
```

`chunks()` never yields an empty slice, so `s == ""` sends nothing and returns `OK`.

**Recommended companion: `DiagWriter`.** Slice 5.2's proof is "PM … `diag_print`s the checksum" and 5.7's is "MEM's init `diag_print`s image size" — both need number formatting, which `&str` alone cannot give in `no_std`. Add in the same file:

```rust
/// A `core::fmt::Write` sink over `diag_print`. Buffers into a
/// `[u8; DIAG_TEXT_MAX]` and flushes on `\n` or when full, so a server can
/// `writeln!(DiagWriter::new(), "checksum={sum:#x}")`.
pub struct DiagWriter { buf: [u8; DIAG_TEXT_MAX], len: usize }
impl DiagWriter { pub fn new() -> Self; pub fn flush(&mut self) -> i32; }
impl core::fmt::Write for DiagWriter { … }
impl Drop for DiagWriter { fn drop(&mut self) { let _ = self.flush(); } }
```

All safe code, ~40 lines, no new dep, and it unblocks 5.2/5.7 without a follow-up. If the PR is getting large, ship `diag_print` alone and defer `DiagWriter` to 5.2 — but 5.2 will need it.

Exports in `server-rt/src/lib.rs`: `mod diag;` beside `mod ds;` (line 36) and `pub use diag::{DiagWriter, diag_print};` beside `pub use ds::sef_publish_to_ds;` (line 41).

**Sonar:** append `server-rt/src/diag.rs` to `sonar.coverage.exclusions` in `sonar-project.properties` (last line), and extend the prose bullet that already names `server-rt/src/ds.rs`. This is required — the module is pure IPC-trap glue and will report 0% coverage otherwise.

## 4. QEMU proof

### 4.1 Which stub, and why

**Stub A**, one-shot prologue. Adding a stub E is out (`NR_STUB_PROCS` feeds `FORK_POOL_BASE` in `servers/pm/src/mproc.rs`, shifting init's children from nr 15 → 16 and breaking three expected markers). Stub A is the right host because:

- Its AS has exactly two mapped pages (`userland.rs:68/71`, `build_stub` at `:478-491`): code RX at `0x0040_0000`, stack RW at `0x0080_0000`, with `sp_el0 = stack_va + PAGE_SIZE = 0x0080_1000` (`userland.rs:505`). Everything else in range is unmapped — clean, predictable targets.
- Stub B (echo server, RECEIVE(ANY) → SEND back) is exactly the partner the deferred path needs, with no change to B at all.
- The expected file carries **no** A-specific behavioral marker (only `[as] stub A nr=11 ttbr0_pa=`), so a prologue can't break an existing assertion.

### 4.2 The asm

Insert at the top of `_user_stub_a_start` (`kernel/src/arch/aarch64/user_stub.S:67`), before `mov x19, #0`:

```asm
    .equ BAD_VA_HI,    0x0090          /* 0x0090_0000 — in range, unmapped in A's AS */
    .equ STRADDLE_VA,  0x0FF8          /* stack page + 0xFF8: 8 good bytes, 96 in the next (unmapped) page */

_user_stub_a_start:
    /* ---- slice 5.1 one-shot fault-safety probes (run once, then fall
     *      into the ping-pong loop unchanged) ------------------------ */

    /* (1) immediate read path: SEND whose message pointer is in range but
     *     unmapped. copy_msg_from_user's PT walk misses -> EFAULT in x0.
     *     mini_send copies BEFORE it inspects the destination
     *     (ipc/send.rs:75 precedes the will_receive check at :85), so A is
     *     never queued and B is never involved. */
    movz    x9, #BAD_VA_HI, lsl #16
    mov     x0, #ENDPOINT_B
    mov     x1, #SEND
    mov     x2, x9
    svc     #0                              /* x0 == EFAULT(-14); kernel traces it */

    /* (2) page-straddle read: 8 bytes land in A's mapped stack page, the
     *     remaining 96 in the unmapped page above it. Proves the chunker
     *     walks page 2 and rejects. */
    movz    x10, #0x0080, lsl #16
    movk    x10, #STRADDLE_VA               /* 0x0080_0FF8 */
    mov     x0, #ENDPOINT_B
    mov     x1, #SEND
    mov     x2, x10
    svc     #0                              /* x0 == EFAULT(-14) */

    /* (3) deferred write path: a good SEND, then a RECEIVE naming a bad
     *     deliver buffer. mini_receive records deliver_msg_vir (receive.rs:64)
     *     and never copies; flush_deliver_msg walks it later and patches
     *     EFAULT into A's parked x0. */
    sub     x11, sp, #MSG_SIZE
    str     wzr, [x11, #0]
    str     wzr, [x11, #4]
    mov     x0, #ENDPOINT_B
    mov     x1, #SEND
    mov     x2, x11
    svc     #0                              /* good buffer: delivers or queues */
    mov     x0, #ENDPOINT_B
    mov     x1, #RECEIVE
    mov     x2, x9                          /* 0x0090_0000 — bad deliver buffer */
    svc     #0                              /* returns EFAULT via the flush */

    mov     x19, #0                         /* persistent message counter */
1:
    /* ... existing ping-pong loop, unchanged ... */
```

**Probe (3) is deferred under either scheduling order** — I traced both:

- *A runs first.* B has not yet executed its first RECEIVE, so B is runnable, `will_receive(B, A)` is false, and A's SEND **blocks** on B's `caller_q`. B runs, RECEIVEs, gets A's message, then SENDs the echo back — but A is now merely runnable, so B's SEND queues on A's `caller_q`. A resumes from SEND and its `RECEIVE(B, bad)` finds B via `walk_caller_q` (receive.rs:155), sets `MF_DELIVERMSG` and returns `OK`. Then `el1_svc_tail` → `schedule_next` → `flush_deliver_msg` fails and overwrites `x0` with EFAULT in the same trap.
- *B runs first (already RECEIVE(ANY)-blocked).* A's SEND delivers immediately (send.rs:85-93); A stays running and its `RECEIVE(B, bad)` finds nothing, records `deliver_msg_vir`, and blocks. B then runs and its echo SEND sets `MF_DELIVERMSG` + `rts_unset(RTS_RECEIVING)`. A is picked later and the flush fails, patching A's parked `x0`.

Either way `flush_deliver_msg` is the code under test — the second case is the genuinely-deferred, different-proc one, which is why the TTBR0-ordering constraint mattered.

**No deadlock.** I walked `deadlock_check` (`kernel/src/ipc/deadlock.rs:30-93`) for `RECEIVE(A→B)`: at `group == 2` the size-2 escape doesn't fire, then B's blocked-on edge either terminates (B runnable → `return false` at line 77) or is `ANY`, which decodes to no live proc. Same shape as A's existing SENDREC receive half, so no new behavior. In the *A-runs-first* ordering the queued-sender match at receive.rs:85 short-circuits before `deadlock_check` runs at all.

**Blob size:** ~20 added instructions ≈ 80 bytes. `copy_stub_into_frame` asserts `len <= PAGE_SIZE` (`userland.rs:532`); A's blob is currently ~50 bytes. No concern.

**Optional 4th probe — RO-page write rejection.** `RECEIVE(B, 0x0040_0000)` (A's `Prot::RO_CODE` code page) exercises `copy_to_user_as`'s `prot.writable` check, which otherwise has no coverage anywhere. Costs 5 instructions and a second SEND/RECEIVE pair. Include it if the prologue stays readable; it produces a third `[deliver efault]` line with `va=0x400000`.

## 5. Risk list

**Regression risks to existing boot markers**

1. **`[ipc N]` / `[ksys N]` counter shift.** Six new `diag_print` SENDRECs at boot bump `ipc::CALL_COUNT` (`ipc/mod.rs:54`) and `system::CALL_COUNT` (`system/mod.rs:80`), changing which calls land in `TRACE_HEAD = 24` and which hit the every-100 sampler. **Verified safe:** `tests/qemu-boot.expected` contains *no* counter-keyed marker. Its only counted line, `[alarm 1] owner=r nr=2 at=`, uses the independent `ALARM_COUNT` (`ipc/mod.rs:327`); `[ksys SYS_FORK/EXEC/EXIT/KILL]` use per-handler head-carved counters, not the `[ksys N]` sampler. Still the #1 thing to re-verify after the first QEMU run.
2. **Write-permission check breaks a legitimate delivery.** If any proc's `deliver_msg_vir` points at a page mapped read-only, delivery now EFAULTs where it previously succeeded. Audited: every server's `Message` is a stack local (`servers/ds/src/main.rs:69`, and the same shape in vm/pm/rs/sched/vfs) on the RW `SERVER_STACK_VA` page; stubs carve from `SP_EL0`; init/worker likewise. **Verification:** watch for any `[deliver efault]` line other than `nr=11` in the boot log — that's the canary.
3. **Stub A prologue changes A/B's first exchanges.** B's first echo lands in a bad buffer and is dropped; A's counter still starts at 0 and the ping-pong loop is byte-identical. Nothing asserts on A's IPC content. Verify A keeps producing `[ipc N] caller=11` lines after the probes.
4. **Marker brittleness.** `[ipc efault] caller=11 call=1 va=` embeds stub A's fixed slot (11) and `SEND` (1) — both structural constants. Deliberately stopping the substring before `va=`'s value keeps `USER_STACK_VA_A`/`USER_CODE_VA_A` refactorable without touching the expected file.
5. **`--no-default-features`.** Probes and their two markers vanish with `boot-stubs` off. CI's `qemu-smoke` only boots the default config, so no gate breaks — but all new asm/consts must sit inside `#[cfg(feature = "boot-stubs")]` / be dropped with `user_stub.S` by `kernel/build.rs`, or the blocking `clippy-kernel --no-default-features` job goes red.

**CI gate risks**

6. **`clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`** — `kernel-shared`'s new `page_chunks` gets linted in its *std test* config too (CLAUDE.md line 171): use module-level `const _: () = assert!(…)` not bare `assert!(CONST op CONST)`, and `assert_eq!` inside `#[test]` fns. Extract `trace_ipc_efault` / `trace_deliver_efault` helpers the way `trace_alarm_fire` (`ipc/mod.rs:382`) already does. Every new `unsafe` block in `mm/uaccess.rs` needs its `// SAFETY:` comment (CLAUDE.md line 145).

**Correctness risks in the new code**

12. **Partial write on a straddling buffer** — mitigated by probe-first in `copy_to_user_as`. If that pre-pass is dropped for performance later, the EFAULT contract silently weakens; document it at the function.
13. **`ttbr0_pa == 0`** — a new class of bug the old live-TTBR0 code could not have. `walk_pt_in(0, …)` would read PA 0 through HHDM. Guard in both `walk_pt_in` and the two `copy_*_user_as` entry points. Note `sched.rs:313` is a `debug_assert!` and is compiled out (release-only kernel, CLAUDE.md line 144) — do not rely on it.
14. **HHDM/TTBR0 alias coherency** — the one non-obvious correctness question. Both mappings are Normal-WB Inner-Shareable (`ATTR_IDX_NORMAL`, `addrspace.rs:68`) and ARMv8 D-caches are PIPT, so no maintenance is required. `addrspace::table_mut` already depends on exactly this for live page tables. Write it into the `// SAFETY:` comment so a future reader doesn't "fix" it.

3	//! `SYS_SETALARM` — arm a per-process one-shot timer (slice 4.4).
4	//!
5	//! Replaces the slice-2.6 `ENOSYS` placeholder. The caller asks for a timer a
6	//! relative number of clock ticks in the future; the kernel records an absolute
7	//! deadline on the caller's [`Proc::alarm_at`] and folds it into the
8	//! `clock::EARLIEST_ALARM` fast-path gate. On the tick where the deadline is
9	//! reached, `clock::tick` → [`crate::ipc::fire_expired_alarms`] delivers a
10	//! kernel-originated `NOTIFY` from `CLOCK` to the owner and disarms the timer.
11	//! A periodic alarm is just a re-arm on each fire (what RS does).
12	//!
13	//! This is a *caller-local* kernel call — it acts only on the caller, never a
14	//! target named in the message — so it takes a single `&mut Proc` and is
15	//! dispatched through [`dispatch_caller_local`](super::dispatch_caller_local),
16	//! unlike the target-taking `do_vmctl` / `do_schedule`.
17	//!
18	//! ## Message payload layout (offsets within `Message::payload`)
19	//!
20	//! | offset | field                         | direction |
21	//! |--------|-------------------------------|-----------|
22	//! |  0..8  | delta ticks (u64); 0 = cancel | in        |
23	//! |  0..8  | previous time-left (u64)      | out       |
24	//!
25	//! Returning the previous timer's remaining ticks mirrors MINIX 3's
26	//! `SYS_SETALARM` reply (`m_lsys_krn_sys_setalarm.time_left`). RS ignores it.
27	//!
28	//! [`Proc::alarm_at`]: crate::proc::Proc::alarm_at
29	
30	use minixrs_kernel_shared::error::OK;
31	use minixrs_kernel_shared::message::Message;
32	
33	use crate::clock;
34	use crate::proc::{Priv, Proc};
35	
36	/// `SYS_SETALARM`. Arms (or cancels, when `delta == 0`) the caller's one-shot
37	/// alarm and replies with the previous timer's remaining ticks.
38	pub(super) fn do_setalarm(caller: &mut Proc, _caller_priv: &Priv, msg: &mut Message) -> i32 {
39	    let delta = read_u64(msg, 0);
40	    let now = clock::uptime();
41	
42	    // Previous timer's remaining ticks (0 if it was disarmed or already due).
43	    let prev_remaining = caller.alarm_at.saturating_sub(now);
44	
45	    if delta == 0 {
46	        // Cancel. The stale `alarm_at` is left in `EARLIEST_ALARM`'s cached
47	        // minimum, but `fire_expired_alarms` recomputes the gate from the live
48	        // `alarm_at` fields on the next fire, so a cancelled timer simply never
49	        // fires (its slot reads `alarm_at == 0`).
50	        caller.alarm_at = 0;
51	    } else {
52	        let at = now.saturating_add(delta);
53	        caller.alarm_at = at;
54	        clock::arm_alarm(at);
55	    }
56	
57	    write_u64(msg, 0, prev_remaining);
58	    OK
59	}

    /* ---- slice 5.1: one-shot fault-safety probes ------------------------
     * Three deliberate bad-pointer IPCs, run once before the ping-pong loop.
     * Each must come back EFAULT (-14) in x0 with the kernel still standing;
     * before slice 5.1 the first one took an EL1 data abort and panicked.
     * The kernel traces each as an `[efault ...]` line -- the checked-in
     * boot markers for this slice.
     */

    /* (1) immediate read path: SEND whose message pointer is unmapped.
     *     `mini_send` copies the message before it inspects the destination,
     *     so B is never involved and A is never queued. */
    movz    x9, #BAD_VA_HI, lsl #16         // 0x0090_0000
    mov     x0, #ENDPOINT_B
    mov     x1, #SEND
    mov     x2, x9
    svc     #0                              // -> x0 == EFAULT

    /* (2) page-straddling read: 8 bytes land in A's mapped stack page, the
     *     other 96 in the unmapped page above it. A Message is only
     *     8-aligned, so this really can happen; it proves the copy engine
     *     walks *every* page of the range, not just the first. */
    movz    x10, #STACK_VA_HI, lsl #16
    movk    x10, #STRADDLE_LO               // 0x0080_0FF8
    mov     x0, #ENDPOINT_B
    mov     x1, #SEND
    mov     x2, x10
    svc     #0                              // -> x0 == EFAULT

     *     deliver buffer. `mini_receive` only records the buffer VA; B's
     *     echo is deposited via MF_DELIVERMSG and the *flush* discovers the
     *     bad page, patching EFAULT into A's parked x0. Works under either
     *     scheduling order -- if B is already RECEIVE-blocked the echo
     *     arrives while A is blocked; otherwise A's RECEIVE finds B queued
     *     on its caller_q. Either way the flush is the code under test. */

    str     wzr, [x11, #0]                  // m_source -- kernel overwrites
    str     wzr, [x11, #4]                  // m_type = 0
    mov     x0, #ENDPOINT_B
    mov     x1, #SEND
    mov     x2, x11
    svc     #0                              // good buffer: delivers or queues
    mov     x0, #ENDPOINT_B
    mov     x1, #RECEIVE
    mov     x2, x9                          // bad deliver buffer
    svc     #0                              // -> x0 == EFAULT, via the flush

    /* A's next SENDREC re-records a good deliver_msg_vir, so the probes
     * leave no lasting state and the loop below is unchanged. */

273	/// Pick the highest-priority runnable process, park its register frame in
274	/// `TPIDR_EL1`, and flush any pending `MF_DELIVERMSG` into its user
275	/// buffer. Called at every EL1 → EL0 transition (SVC tail, IRQ tail,
276	/// first-dispatch from `run`).
277	///
278	/// Does *not* touch the run queue — `rts_set`/`rts_unset` keep blocked
279	/// procs off, and `reschedule` handles the quantum-rotation case
280	/// separately. If `pick_proc` finds nothing runnable, the previous
281	/// current stays current.
282	///
283	/// TODO(slice 2.6+): once IDLE is enqueued at boot, an empty run queue
284	/// becomes an invariant violation rather than the expected
285	/// "both-stubs-briefly-blocked" state we see in slice 2.5. At that
286	/// point, add `debug_assert!(pick_proc().is_some(), "run queue empty
287	/// — IDLE missing?")` so a regression that dequeues IDLE blows up
288	/// loudly. Today only stubs A/B are enqueued (see
289	/// `arch/aarch64/userland.rs::userland_bootstrap`), so the assert
290	/// would fire spuriously.
291	///
292	/// SAFETY: caller must hold the single-threaded / IRQ-masked invariant
293	/// and must not hold any other reference into `PROC_TABLE` while this
294	/// runs.
295	pub unsafe fn schedule_next() {
296	    let next_nr = match pick_proc() {
297	        Some(nr) => nr,
298	        None => return,
299	    };
300	    CURRENT_PROC_NR.store(next_nr.get(), Ordering::Relaxed);
301	    // SAFETY: next_nr came from the run queue; single-borrow.
302	    unsafe {
303	        let next = proc_slot_mut(next_nr).expect("schedule_next: next out of range");
304	        set_tpidr_to(next);
305	        // Per-proc TTBR0 + ASID install. Slice 3.1b: every runnable proc
306	        // is an EL0 stub with a real address space. This debug_assert gives
307	        // a richer per-proc message in debug builds; the authoritative
308	        // guard against a kernel task (asid=0) silently installing
309	        // TTBR0_EL1 = 0 lives in `switch_ttbr0_with_asid`, which asserts
310	        // unconditionally (the kernel only builds --release). The TTBR0
311	        // swap must happen *before* `flush_deliver_msg` — the flush writes
312	        // via the active TTBR0, so the new proc's AS must already be live.
313	        debug_assert!(
314	            next.ttbr0_pa != 0 && next.asid != 0,
315	            "schedule_next: proc nr={} has no AS (ttbr0_pa={:#x}, asid={})",
316	            next.nr.get(),
317	            next.ttbr0_pa,
318	            next.asid,
319	        );
320	        crate::arch::aarch64::mmu::switch_ttbr0_with_asid(next.ttbr0_pa, next.asid);
321	        crate::ipc::flush_deliver_msg(next);
322	    }
323	}

10	//! let sef = sef_startup(SefConfig { init_fresh: Some(my_init), signal_handler: None })?;
11	//! let mut msg = Message { m_source: 0, m_type: 0, payload: [0u8; 96] };
12	//! loop {
13	//!     if sef.receive(&mut msg) != 0 { continue; }
14	//!     match msg.m_type { /* application requests */ }
15	//! }
16	//! ```
17	//!
18	//! [`sef_startup`] learns the server's own endpoint + name via
19	//! `SYS_GETINFO(GET_WHOAMI)` and runs the registered fresh-init callback.
20	//! [`Sef::receive`] wraps `ipc_receive(ANY, …)` and transparently handles SEF
21	//! control messages (RS heartbeat pings, signals, re-init), returning only
22	//! application traffic to the server.

25	//! [`SefConfig`] and carried in the returned [`Sef`] handle — no static mutable
26	//! state, so the whole crate is `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` (all `unsafe` lives in
27	//! `minix-ipc`). Live-update / state-transfer SEF features are deferred.

c-headers:
    name: generated C headers
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Blocking (phase-5 decision D8): the generated headers are the musl fork's
    # only view of the minix.rs ABI, and they are never committed — so a Rust
    # change that produces uncompilable C has to fail in the slice that made it,
    # not in slice 5.6 when the first C file appears.
    #
    # No clang install step: kernel/build.rs already shells out to bare `clang`
    # to assemble the kernel's .S files, so it is an existing hard build
    # requirement that the runner images satisfy.
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6.0.3
      - name: Install pinned toolchain
        run: rustup show
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@e18b497796c12c097a38f9edb9d0641fb99eee32 # v2
      - name: Generate headers
        run: cargo gen-c-headers
      # -nostdlibinc (clang-only; do not "portably" swap in cc) plus
      # -ffreestanding keeps the check hermetic: the selftest sees ONLY the
      # generated headers and clang's own resource-dir headers, so it cannot
      # accidentally validate against the host libc — whose errno values differ
      # from musl's (Darwin EDEADLK is 11, not 35). Three triples: the host
      # proves portability, the two musl triples are what actually ships.
      # -fsyntax-only needs no backend, no linker, and no sysroot.
      - name: Syntax-check the generated headers
        run: |
          for target in "" "--target=aarch64-unknown-linux-musl" \
                           "--target=x86_64-unknown-linux-musl"; do
            clang -std=c11 -pedantic-errors -Wall -Wextra -Werror \
              -fsyntax-only -ffreestanding -nostdlibinc $target \
              -Itarget/gen-c-headers/include \
              target/gen-c-headers/abi-selftest.c
          done
      # Compiles <minix/errno.h>'s opt-in POSIX block against the generated
      # stand-in. A syntax and macro-spelling check only — the stand-in is
      # generated from the same Rust table the assertions check. The real value
      # check runs against the musl fork's bits/errno.h from slice 5.6 on.
      - name: Syntax-check the opt-in errno assertions
        run: |
          clang -std=c11 -pedantic-errors -Wall -Wextra -Werror \
            -fsyntax-only -ffreestanding -nostdlibinc \
            --target=aarch64-unknown-linux-musl \
            -DMINIX_ABI_CHECK_POSIX_ERRNO \
            -Itarget/gen-c-headers/abi-check \
            -Itarget/gen-c-headers/include \
            target/gen-c-headers/abi-selftest.c
      # D8: the headers are build artifacts under target/ and are never
      # committed. Makes that rule mechanical rather than a convention.
      - name: Assert nothing was written into the tree
        run: |
          git diff --exit-code
          test -z "$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all)"

12	/// The 18 kernel calls, in numeric order.
13	fn kernel_calls() -> [(&'static str, i32); 18] {
14	    [
15	        ("SYS_GETINFO", callnr::SYS_GETINFO),
16	        ("SYS_PRIVCTL", callnr::SYS_PRIVCTL),
17	        ("SYS_FORK", callnr::SYS_FORK),
18	        ("SYS_EXEC", callnr::SYS_EXEC),
19	        ("SYS_EXIT", callnr::SYS_EXIT),
20	        ("SYS_COPY", callnr::SYS_COPY),
21	        ("SYS_SAFECOPY", callnr::SYS_SAFECOPY),
22	        ("SYS_IRQCTL", callnr::SYS_IRQCTL),
23	        ("SYS_VMCTL", callnr::SYS_VMCTL),
24	        ("SYS_SCHEDULE", callnr::SYS_SCHEDULE),
25	        ("SYS_SETALARM", callnr::SYS_SETALARM),
26	        ("SYS_TIMES", callnr::SYS_TIMES),
27	        ("SYS_DIAGCTL", callnr::SYS_DIAGCTL),
28	        ("SYS_SETGRANT", callnr::SYS_SETGRANT),
29	        ("SYS_SCHEDCTL", callnr::SYS_SCHEDCTL),
30	        ("SYS_KILL", callnr::SYS_KILL),
31	        ("SYS_GETKSIG", callnr::SYS_GETKSIG),
32	        ("SYS_ENDKSIG", callnr::SYS_ENDKSIG),
33	    ]
34	}
35	
36	/// A server request band: base constant, its members, and the count constant
37	/// that bounds it (`None` for VM, which has no `NR_*` on the Rust side).
38	///
39	/// `members` is checked against `count` by
40	/// `every_band_member_list_matches_its_count`: a new request that bumps the Rust
41	/// `NR_*` without gaining a row here would otherwise render a larger count and
42	/// no macro for the request itself.
43	struct Band {
44	    title: &'static str,
45	    base_name: &'static str,
46	    base: i32,
47	    count: Option<(&'static str, usize)>,
48	    members: Vec<(&'static str, i32)>,
49	}
50	
51	fn bands() -> [Band; 5] {
52	    [
53	        Band {
54	            title: "PM requests",
55	            base_name: "PM_RQ_BASE",
56	            base: callnr::PM_RQ_BASE,
57	            count: Some(("NR_PM_MSGS", callnr::NR_PM_MSGS)),
58	            members: vec![
59	                ("PM_GETPID", callnr::PM_GETPID),
60	                ("PM_FORK", callnr::PM_FORK),
61	                ("PM_EXIT", callnr::PM_EXIT),
62	                ("PM_WAIT", callnr::PM_WAIT),
63	                ("PM_EXEC", callnr::PM_EXEC),
64	            ],
65	        },
66	        Band {
67	            title: "VM requests",
68	            base_name: "VM_RQ_BASE",
69	            base: callnr::VM_RQ_BASE,
70	            count: None,
71	            members: vec![
72	                ("VM_PAGEFAULT", callnr::VM_PAGEFAULT),
73	                ("VM_BRK", callnr::VM_BRK),
74	                ("VM_MMAP", callnr::VM_MMAP),
75	                ("VM_MUNMAP", callnr::VM_MUNMAP),
76	                ("VM_FORK", callnr::VM_FORK),
77	            ],
78	        },
79	        Band {
80	            title: "SEF control messages",
81	            base_name: "SEF_RQ_BASE",
82	            base: callnr::SEF_RQ_BASE,
83	            count: Some(("NR_SEF_MSGS", callnr::NR_SEF_MSGS)),
84	            members: vec![
85	                ("SEF_INIT", callnr::SEF_INIT),
86	                ("SEF_SIGNAL", callnr::SEF_SIGNAL),
87	            ],
88	        },
89	        Band {
90	            title: "DS requests",
91	            base_name: "DS_RQ_BASE",
92	            base: callnr::DS_RQ_BASE,
93	            count: Some(("NR_DS_REQUESTS", callnr::NR_DS_REQUESTS)),
94	            members: vec![
95	                ("DS_PUBLISH", callnr::DS_PUBLISH),
96	                ("DS_RETRIEVE", callnr::DS_RETRIEVE),
97	                ("DS_CHECK", callnr::DS_CHECK),
98	            ],
99	        },
100	        Band {
101	            title: "SCHED requests",
102	            base_name: "SCHED_RQ_BASE",
103	            base: callnr::SCHED_RQ_BASE,
104	            count: Some(("NR_SCHED_MSGS", callnr::NR_SCHED_MSGS)),
105	            members: vec![
106	                ("SCHEDULING_NO_QUANTUM", callnr::SCHEDULING_NO_QUANTUM),
107	                ("SCHEDULING_START", callnr::SCHEDULING_START),
108	                ("SCHEDULING_STOP", callnr::SCHEDULING_STOP),
109	                ("SCHEDULING_SET_NICE", callnr::SCHEDULING_SET_NICE),
110	            ],
111	        },
112	    ]
113	}

115	/// Render `minix/callnr.h`.
116	pub fn render() -> String {
117	    let mut f = CFile::new(
118	        "Kernel-call numbers, server request bands, and their payload constants.",
119	        &["kernel-shared/src/callnr.rs"],
120	    );
121	    f.guard_open(GUARD);
122	
123	    f.blank();
124	    f.include(
125	        "minix/ipc.h",
126	        "NOTIFY_MESSAGE, for the band ordering checks",
127	    );
128	
129	    f.block_comment(&[
130	        "Deviation from MINIX 3: its <minix/callnr.h> holds POSIX syscall numbers",
131	        "and keeps server request numbers in <minix/com.h>. minix.rs has no POSIX",
132	        "call-number layer -- a libc wrapper builds a server request directly --",
133	        "so this header carries the kernel calls and the request bands together.",
134	        "",
135	        "Payload byte offsets are not emitted yet: on the Rust side they live in",
136	        "doc comments rather than constants. The first musl wrapper (slice 5.6) is",
137	        "the forcing function for promoting them to real constants.",
138	    ]);
139	
140	    f.section("kernel calls");
141	    f.define_hex("KERNEL_CALL", callnr::KERNEL_CALL.into());
142	    f.blank();
143	    for (name, value) in kernel_calls() {
144	        f.define_hex(name, value.into());
145	    }
146	    f.blank();
147	    f.define_raw(
148	        "NR_KERN_CALLS",
149	        &format!(
150	            "{}   /* kernel-shared: NR_KERN_CALLS_PHASE4 */",
151	            callnr::NR_KERN_CALLS_PHASE4
152	        ),
153	    );
154	    f.define_dec("NR_SYS_CALLS", callnr::NR_SYS_CALLS as i64);
155	
156	    f.section("kernel-call payload constants");
157	    f.define_dec("GET_WHOAMI", callnr::GET_WHOAMI.into());
158	    f.define_dec("SYS_GETINFO_NAME_LEN", callnr::SYS_GETINFO_NAME_LEN as i64);
159	    f.define_dec("EXEC_NAME_LEN", callnr::EXEC_NAME_LEN as i64);
160	    f.define_dec("PRIVCTL_SET_USER", callnr::PRIVCTL_SET_USER.into());
161	    f.define_dec("SCHEDCTL_FLAG_KERNEL", callnr::SCHEDCTL_FLAG_KERNEL.into());
162	
163	    f.section("SYS_DIAGCTL subcodes + inline-text payload");
164	    f.define_dec("DIAGCTL_CODE_DIAG", callnr::DIAGCTL_CODE_DIAG.into());
165	    f.define_dec(
166	        "DIAGCTL_CODE_STACKTRACE",
167	        callnr::DIAGCTL_CODE_STACKTRACE.into(),
168	    );
169	    f.define_dec(
170	        "DIAGCTL_CODE_REGISTER",
171	        callnr::DIAGCTL_CODE_REGISTER.into(),
172	    );
173	    f.define_dec(
174	        "DIAGCTL_CODE_UNREGISTER",
175	        callnr::DIAGCTL_CODE_UNREGISTER.into(),
176	    );
177	    f.define_dec("DIAG_TEXT_OFF", callnr::DIAG_TEXT_OFF as i64);
178	    f.define_dec("DIAG_TEXT_MAX", callnr::DIAG_TEXT_MAX as i64);
179	
180	    f.section("SYS_VMCTL subcalls");
181	    f.define_dec("VMCTL_PT_MAP", callnr::VMCTL_PT_MAP.into());
182	    f.define_dec("VMCTL_PT_UNMAP", callnr::VMCTL_PT_UNMAP.into());
183	    f.define_dec(

185	        callnr::VMCTL_CLEAR_PAGEFAULT.into(),
186	    );

188	    f.define_dec("VMCTL_VMINHIBIT_SET", callnr::VMCTL_VMINHIBIT_SET.into());

### `SYS_VMCTL` subcalls

`SYS_VMCTL` is VM's single privileged lever over the kernel's paging mechanism.
The subcall selector is in the first payload word; the target process (endpoint,
`SELF` allowed) in the next. Numbers start at 1 so a zeroed payload is invalid.

| Subcall | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| `VMCTL_PT_MAP` (1) | Allocate a fresh zeroed frame, map it at `vaddr`, reply with the PA. |
| `VMCTL_PT_UNMAP` (2) | Unmap `vaddr` and free the frame (`EINVAL` if nothing mapped). |
| `VMCTL_CLEAR_PAGEFAULT` (3) | Clear a recorded fault and make the target runnable. |

### `SYS_DIAGCTL` subcodes

`SYS_DIAGCTL` is the servers' debug channel. Servers run at EL0 with no console
of their own, so without it their behavior is only observable indirectly, through
kernel-side traces. `server-rt::diag_print` is the client side.

Unlike MINIX 3, which passes a `(buf, len)` user pointer and copies the text in,
minix.rs carries the text **inline in the message payload**: the subcode in
payload `0..4`, the length in `4..8`, and up to `DIAG_TEXT_MAX` (88) text bytes
from `DIAG_TEXT_OFF` (8). The channel therefore needs no user-copy machinery and
cannot fault — it has to keep working while the copy engine and grants are
themselves under construction. `diag_print` splits longer strings across
successive calls, one console line each.

| Subcode | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| `DIAGCTL_CODE_DIAG` (1) | Print the inline text as one `[diag <name>] …` line. |
| `DIAGCTL_CODE_STACKTRACE` (2) | Reserved (MINIX 3) — `EINVAL`. |
| `DIAGCTL_CODE_REGISTER` / `_UNREGISTER` (3/4) | Reserved (MINIX 3 kernel-message subscription) — `EINVAL`. |

The `<name>` prefix is the caller's name as the *kernel* knows it, never
anything from the payload, so a server can only ever identify itself. Text is
restricted to printable ASCII, which keeps one call to exactly one line — the
boot-marker checks in `tests/qemu-boot.expected` depend on that framing. No extra
privilege gate is needed: `Priv::k_call_mask` already limits kernel calls to
server-grade privileges, and the shared USER privilege has an empty mask, so
ordinary user processes cannot reach this call.

### Slice 5.1: fault-safe user copy + real `SYS_DIAGCTL` ◀ ready (branch `feature/slice-5.1-uaccess-diagctl`, pending merge)

**Goal:** no user pointer can panic the kernel (D5), and servers can print
(D2) — the observability + safety floor for everything after.

**Scope:** replace `copy_msg_from_user`/`copy_msg_to_user` with PT-walk +
HHDM copies against the caller's (resp. receiver's) address space; `EFAULT`
to the caller's `x0` on send/kernel-call request/reply, `EFAULT` to the
receiver's parked `x0` when the deferred `flush_deliver_msg` hits a bad
deliver buffer (replacing the silent `let _ =`). `SYS_DIAGCTL` body:
inline-payload text (len + bytes in the 96-byte payload), kernel writes it
to the UART with a `[diag <name>]`-style prefix; `server-rt` gains a
`diag_print` helper that chunks longer strings. Drive-bys nominated by
`phase-5-prep.md` for the first PR touching these files: stale era comments
in `kernel/src/ipc/{message.rs,senda.rs,mod.rs}`, and `ipc_const.rs`'s wrong
"`x16`" trap-ABI comment (the real register is `x1`).

**Proof:** a one-shot deliberate bad-pointer IPC from the stub battery
(boot-stubs-gated) traces `result=-14` (`EFAULT` at its final 5.0 value)
with no panic; a server's `diag_print` line appears in the boot log and
joins `tests/qemu-boot.expected`.

**As built** (differences from the sketch above, recorded so later slices do
not rediscover them):

- The copy engine is a **general byte-level module**, `kernel/src/mm/uaccess.rs`
  (`copy_from_user_as` / `copy_to_user_as` / `probe_user_range`, all over a raw
  `ttbr0_pa`), not message-specific helpers. Slice 5.2's grant engine builds on
  it directly — a cross-AS copy is two walks and a `memcpy`. `addrspace.rs`
  gains the missing member of its `*_in` free-function family,
  `walk_pt_in(ttbr0_pa, va) -> Option<(u64, Prot)>`; `AddrSpace::walk_pt`
  delegates to it. The `Prot` half is load-bearing: the kernel copies through
  the HHDM alias, which the MMU's EL0 permission bits do **not** police, so
  `copy_to_user_as` must reject a read-only destination explicitly.
- **Writes are all-or-nothing** (`probe_user_range` first). A 104-byte `Message`
  is only 8-aligned and really can straddle two pages, so copy-as-you-go would
  leave a half-written message in a user buffer before returning `EFAULT`.
- The page-split arithmetic lives in `kernel-shared` as `page_chunks` /
  `PageChunk` / `USER_PAGE_SIZE` beside `user_va_ok`, with 6 host tests — the
  kernel crate has no `#[cfg(test)]`, and this is the one piece of the slice
  with real off-by-one risk. `kernel-shared` goes 60 → 68 tests.
- `ipc/message.rs` ends with **zero `unsafe`**: messages stage through a
  `[u8; 104]` and are reassembled field-by-field, so every raw-pointer operation
  in the user-copy path is in `mm::uaccess` alone.
- `MF_MSGFAILED` already existed in `proc/flags.rs` (unused since Phase 2); the
  flush now sets *and clears* it, so it records "the last delivery to this proc
  failed" rather than being write-only. Nothing reads it yet — a later signals
  slice can turn it into `SIGSEGV`, which is what MINIX's `delivermsg()` does.
- Traces are **uncounted**, unlike the sampled `[ipc {n}]` form, so they are
  stable boot markers: `[efault] proc=A nr=11 call=1 va=…` (emitted in `do_ipc`
  keyed on `result == EFAULT`, which covers all three immediate copy sites at
  once — nothing else in the kernel produces `EFAULT`) and
  `[efault deliver] proc=A nr=11 va=…`.
- **Three** probes on stub A's prologue, not one — an unmapped page, a
  *page-straddling* buffer (8 bytes in A's stack page, 96 in the unmapped page
  above), and the deferred-flush path. A new stub E was rejected:
  `NR_STUB_PROCS` feeds `FORK_POOL_BASE`, so a fifth stub would shift init's
  forked children 15 → 16 and break three existing markers.
- `SYS_DIAGCTL` takes a **subcode** (`DIAGCTL_CODE_DIAG = 1`, MINIX 3's
  numbering, with 2–4 reserved and `EINVAL`), so text budget is
  `DIAG_TEXT_MAX = 88` after the subcode and length words. Text is sanitized to
  printable ASCII, which is what guarantees one call = one line and keeps the
  `grep -aF` marker contract intact.
- `diag_print` is called from **`sef_startup`**, so all six SEF servers announce
  themselves (`[diag vm] sef ready`, …) for one line of code. Two are asserted
  as markers. It is placed before the `init_fresh` callback so the line proves
  `SYS_DIAGCTL` independently of DS.
- Done here rather than deferred: the `NR_KERN_CALLS_PHASE4` → `NR_KERN_CALLS`
  rename (25 references; the C header already emitted the un-suffixed name, and
  a `nr_kern_calls_is_not_phase_suffixed` test now forbids any phase-scoped name
  in the ABI header). The `sef.receive(…) != 0` → `!= OK` sweep was **5** sites,
  not the 9 slice 5.0 estimated — `drivers/`, `fs/` and `userland/` have no
  receive loops yet. VFS's `let _ = sef.receive(…)` is left alone: it discards
  every message, so the discard is the honest form.
- `tests/qemu-boot.forbidden` gains `!!! kernel exception (vector index` — the
  same-EL banner, which is precisely what a kernel dereference of a bad user
  pointer produced before this slice. `!!! KERNEL PANIC:` already caught it
  transitively, but this is the sharper canary.
- **Verification note for future slices:** the highest risk was *surfacing* a
  previously-silent failure — kernel-originated notifies (`deliver_alarm`,
  `deliver_ksig`, `mini_pf_send`, `send_no_quantum`) set `MF_DELIVERMSG` on a
  proc whose `deliver_msg_vir` came from its own last RECEIVE, and the old
  `let _ =` swallowed a bad one. The guard is a **stub-free boot**
  (`--no-default-features`) grepped for `[efault]`: it must be empty. It is.

- **Fault-safe user access + the debug channel (slice 5.1):** the kernel **never dereferences a user VA**, not even the active TTBR0's. Every byte in or out of a user address space goes through `kernel/src/mm/uaccess.rs` — `copy_from_user_as(ttbr0_pa, va, dst)` / `copy_to_user_as(ttbr0_pa, va, src)` / `probe_user_range(ttbr0_pa, va, len, write)` — which page-chunks the range, resolves each page with the new `addrspace::walk_pt_in(ttbr0_pa, va) -> Option<(u64, Prot)>` (the missing member of the `map_page_in`/`unmap_page_in`/`walk_leaves` free-function family; `AddrSpace::walk_pt` delegates to it), and `memcpy`s through the frame's HHDM alias. Consequences to preserve: an unmapped page is a walk miss returning **`EFAULT`, not an EL1 abort** — so **no exception-fixup table is needed or wanted** (D5 rejected the Linux `extable` approach); the copy is **address-space-independent**, so `flush_deliver_msg` can write a receiver's buffer before its TTBR0 is installed (the TTBR0-before-flush ordering in `sched::schedule_next` is no longer load-bearing, only `eret` needs it); `copy_to_user_as` must **check `Prot::writable`**, because the HHDM alias is a kernel mapping that the MMU's EL0 permission bits do not police; and writes are **all-or-nothing** (probe first) since a 104-byte `Message` is only 8-aligned and really can straddle two pages. Slice 5.2's grant engine builds on these primitives rather than re-deriving them. `user_va_ok` stays as the cheap range/alignment pre-gate; the page arithmetic (`page_chunks` / `PageChunk` / `USER_PAGE_SIZE`) lives in `kernel-shared/src/message.rs` beside it because the kernel crate has no `#[cfg(test)]`. `ipc/message.rs` carries **zero `unsafe`** — messages stage through a `[u8; 104]` — so all raw-pointer work is in `mm::uaccess` alone. Error routing: `EFAULT` to the caller's `x0` via `do_ipc` for the three immediate sites, and to a blocked receiver's **parked `x0`** (`p.regs.x[0] = e as i64 as u64` — the MINIX `retreg` idiom `do_exit::unblock_dependents` uses) for the deferred flush, which also sets/clears the previously-unused `MF_MSGFAILED`. Both traces are **uncounted** (`[efault] proc=… nr=… call=… va=…`, `[efault deliver] proc=… nr=… va=…`) so they are stable boot markers, unlike the sampled `[ipc {n}]` form; the `do_ipc` one keys on `result == EFAULT`, which is unambiguous because nothing else in the kernel produces it. **`SYS_DIAGCTL` is the servers' debug channel** (D2) — servers run at EL0 with no console, and this must keep working while grants/TTY/VFS are under construction, so the text rides **inline in the payload** (subcode `0..4`, len `4..8`, up to `DIAG_TEXT_MAX = 88` bytes from `DIAG_TEXT_OFF = 8`) and needs no user-copy machinery. `kernel/src/system/do_diagctl.rs` prints one line per call as `[diag <name>] <text>`, where `<name>` is the caller's kernel-known `Proc::name` (never payload data, so a server can only identify itself) and text is sanitized to printable ASCII (so one call is always exactly one line — the `grep -aF` marker contract depends on it). `server-rt::diag_print` is the client, chunking longer strings; it is called from **`sef_startup`**, so all six SEF servers emit `[diag <name>] sef ready` at boot. Adding a stub is discouraged: `NR_STUB_PROCS` feeds `FORK_POOL_BASE`, so a fifth stub shifts init's forked children 15 → 16 and breaks checked-in markers — put new probe behavior in an existing stub's prologue (5.1 used stub A's)

content.text:
Slice 5.1 is implemented and verified. Per your auto-mode rule I've stopped short of committing — the changes are on `feature/slice-5.1-uaccess-diagctl`, unstaged, for your review.

## What changed

**Fault-safe user copy (D5).** The kernel no longer dereferences a user VA anywhere. New `kernel/src/mm/uaccess.rs` page-chunks every range, resolves each page via a new `addrspace::walk_pt_in(ttbr0_pa, va) -> Option<(u64, Prot)>` free function, and copies through the frame's HHDM alias. An unmapped page is now a walk miss returning `EFAULT` instead of an EL1 abort that panicked the kernel.

Three refinements beyond the approved plan, all from the design agent's post-approval report:
- **Writes are all-or-nothing** (probe first). A 104-byte `Message` is 8-aligned and really can straddle two pages, so copy-as-you-go would leave a half-written message before returning `EFAULT`.
- `copy_to_user_as` **rejects read-only destinations** — the HHDM alias is a kernel mapping the MMU's EL0 permission bits don't police, so this is a protection bypass the old `write_volatile` never had.
- The deferred flush reuses the **already-existing but unused** `MF_MSGFAILED` flag rather than adding state.

`ipc/message.rs` ends with zero `unsafe`; all raw-pointer work is in `mm::uaccess` alone.

**`SYS_DIAGCTL` (D2).** Real handler with the subcode+len+inline-text layout you picked. `server-rt::diag_print` is called from `sef_startup`, so all six SEF servers announce themselves.

## Verification

- **Default boot:** exit 124, all 30 markers pass (26 pre-existing + 4 new), zero forbidden markers.
- **Stub-free boot** — the highest-risk check, since this slice surfaces a previously-silent failure: **zero** `[efault]` lines, 6 diag lines, 0 panics, 289 healthy init fork/exec/exit cycles. No legitimate flow hits a bad `deliver_msg_vir`.
- Host tests: kernel-shared 60→68, server-rt 9→12, gen-c-headers 50; all other suites unchanged and green.
- `fmt` clean; `clippy --workspace --all-targets`, `clippy -p minixrs-kernel` (both feature configs) clean at `-D warnings`.
- C headers regenerate and pass `-fsyntax-only` on all three triples plus the errno-assertion pass; nothing generated leaked into the tree.

Three things worth flagging:

1. **The `sef.receive(…) != 0` sweep was 5 sites, not 9** — slice 5.0's note was stale; `drivers/`, `fs/` and `userland/` have no receive loops yet. I left VFS's `let _ = sef.receive(…)` alone: it discards every message, so the discard is the honest form rather than an inconsistency.
2. **I used stub A's prologue for three probes, not one** — unmapped page, page-straddling buffer, and the deferred-flush path. A stub E would have shifted `FORK_POOL_BASE` and broken three existing markers.
3. **miri isn't installed on this toolchain**, so I couldn't run it locally. It's advisory in CI, and the new `kernel-shared` code is pure integer arithmetic with no pointers, but it is unverified here.

The `NR_KERN_CALLS_PHASE4` → `NR_KERN_CALLS` rename is mixed into the same working tree rather than isolated — if you want it as a separate commit, I can split it before you commit.

- ELF-only attributes on server crates (`#[unsafe(link_section = ".text._start")]`, etc.) must be `#[cfg_attr(target_os = "none", ...)]`-gated — `cargo check --workspace` also builds servers for the Mach-O host, which rejects ELF section specifiers

- User-space servers run at EL0 with no console access — they cannot print. Verify server behavior through kernel-side traces (`[pf]` from `do_page_fault`, `[ksys …]` from `do_vmctl`/`system`, `[ipc N]` from `ipc::dispatch`), never server-side logging. Trace sampling is asymmetric: `[ipc N]` head-traces the first ~12 calls *plus* every 100th, but `[ksys N]` samples only every 100th (no head carve-out) — a server's first/rare kernel call (e.g. a startup `SYS_GETINFO`) shows on `[ipc]`, not `[ksys]`

- `init_boot_image` fills a boot server's `ipc_to` only for active boot priv slots `[0, n_active)` (~0–15). A hand-installed stub in a higher priv slot (16+) that a server must *reply* to needs the reverse `ipc_to` bit opened explicitly — see `install_stub_d_priv` opening VM→D after setting D→VM

- VM (`servers/vm/`) tracks per-process memory as a static `[ClientRegions; 16]` keyed by proc number (no heap allocator — the kernel owns frames), each region a half-open `[start, end)` tagged `Kind::{Heap, Mmap, Unused}`. A page fault is satisfied only when its address lies inside a region; out-of-region faults are a silent SIGSEGV (faulter left blocked on `RTS_PAGEFAULT` — real signals are Phase 4). `VM_BRK`/`VM_MMAP`/`VM_MUNMAP` all ride the single D→VM SENDREC edge, so adding an mmap client needs no new priv wiring beyond the brk one

- `SYS_VMCTL(VMCTL_PT_UNMAP)` returns `EINVAL` (no panic, no frame freed) when nothing is mapped at the target VA — so VM's `munmap` can sweep a region page-by-page with `VMCTL_PT_UNMAP` and ignore the never-faulted pages. Keep the unmap sweep capped at the region's own `end` so an overstated `len` can't reach a neighbor's frames

content.text:
All four review items are addressed and verified.

**1. Granule coupling** — added `const _: () = assert!(USER_PAGE_SIZE == FRAME_SIZE as u64)` in `uaccess.rs`. I also found the same latent split one level down: `mm::frame::FRAME_SIZE` and `mmu::PAGE_SIZE` are two independent `4096` literals, and `addrspace.rs` mixes them (`check_va` aligns on one, `pte_index` shifts by the other), so it now carries `FRAME_SIZE == PAGE_SIZE` and `1 << PAGE_SHIFT == PAGE_SIZE` too.

**2. Untested `Prot::writable` rejection** — this was the most valuable of the four. Added a fourth stub-A probe: RECEIVE with the deliver buffer naming A's own RO code page. The page is *present*, so the walk succeeds and only the writable check rejects it. I mutation-tested it rather than just asserting it works: stubbing the check to `if false` makes exactly the `va=0x400000` marker vanish and the boot check fail. 31 markers now.

**3. CLAUDE.md `!= 0`** — fixed, and took the opportunity to add the `diag_print` step to that same sentence's description of `sef_startup`.

**4. `try_into().expect(...)`** — I did this one differently than suggested, because the diagnosis was pointing at the wrong hazard. Those `expect`s are unreachable by construction (constant ranges within a constant-size array), and more importantly they'd stay silent in the scenario that actually matters: if `Message` gained a field ahead of `payload`, `PAYLOAD_OFF = 8` would read the wrong 96 bytes, the slice length would still be 96, `try_into` would still *succeed*, and the result is a silent miscopy — no panic to catch. So the real fix is tying the offsets to the layout:

```rust
const _: () = assert!(M_TYPE_OFF == core::mem::offset_of!(Message, m_type));
const _: () = assert!(PAYLOAD_OFF == core::mem::offset_of!(Message, payload));
```

That makes a layout change a compile error, which is what the suggestion asked for. I also took the infallible-indexing half where it's cheap — the two `i32`s are now `from_ne_bytes([buf[0], buf[1], …])` and the payload is `core::array::from_fn`, so all three `expect`s are gone.

**Verification after the changes:** default boot passes all 31 markers; stub-free boot still shows zero spurious `[efault]` lines and no panics; `fmt`, `clippy --workspace --all-targets`, and both kernel clippy configs clean at `-D warnings`; host tests 68/12/50 green.

Still uncommitted on `feature/slice-5.1-uaccess-diagctl` for your review. miri remains the one gate I can't run locally (not installed for this toolchain).

Phase 5's opening slice makes the ABI C-ready before any C exists, so no
later slice bakes a soon-to-change errno into a trace marker or a wrapper.

magnitudes 1..=40, which classic book-era MINIX and musl number
identically (that identity is the point -- musl's stock bits/errno.h and
syscall_ret.c's `r > -4096UL` then work unmodified), and the
MINIX-specific IPC band at >= 200, taking modern MINIX 3
sys/sys/errno.h values. EBADSRCDST is the one name that tree lacks; it
takes the value of its EBADEPT (216). The full contiguous 1..=40 block is
adopted rather than a subset, so no later slice has to add "one more
errno".

positive magnitude and emits both the negated `pub const` and a derived
`pub const ALL: &[(&str, i32)]`. That table is the single source of truth
for the header generator, the compile-time guards, and the host tests --
adding an errno is one line, and a second list cannot drift. `const _`
guards enforce that the POSIX block has no holes, that nothing lands in
the 41..=199 gap where musl defines errnos minix.rs has not adopted, that
values are pairwise distinct, and that OK stays 0.

cat > /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-kevinbarnard-src-minixrs/1d461276-1cf1-4bd5-8638-fd85e783619a/scratchpad/msg.txt <<'EOF'
Slice 5.1: fault-safe user copy + real SYS_DIAGCTL

The safety and observability floor every remaining Phase 5 slice stands
on. Grants (5.2), CDEV/TTY (5.3), VFS (5.4), MFS (5.8) and grant-sourced
exec (5.9) all move user bytes, and all of them need servers that can
speak while that machinery is still half-built.

D5 -- fault-safe user copy. The kernel no longer dereferences a user VA
anywhere, not even the active TTBR0's. New kernel/src/mm/uaccess.rs
page-chunks every range, resolves each page through the new
addrspace::walk_pt_in(ttbr0_pa, va) -> Option<(u64, Prot)> (the missing
member of the map_page_in / unmap_page_in / walk_leaves free-function
family; AddrSpace::walk_pt now delegates to it), and memcpys through the
frame's HHDM alias. An in-range-but-unmapped pointer was previously an
EL1 data abort with no fixup path -- a kernel panic. It is now EFAULT.

Because the walk is address-space-independent, no exception-fixup table
is needed (D5 rejected the Linux extable approach), and the deferred
MF_DELIVERMSG flush can write a receiver's buffer without that receiver's
TTBR0 being installed -- so sched::schedule_next's TTBR0-before-flush
ordering stops being load-bearing; only eret still needs it.

Two properties the old write_volatile got for free and this does not:
copy_to_user_as must check Prot::writable, because the HHDM alias is a
kernel mapping the MMU's EL0 permission bits do not police; and writes
are all-or-nothing (probe_user_range first), because a 104-byte Message
is only 8-aligned and really can straddle two pages, so copy-as-you-go
would leave a half-written message behind on failure.

Error routing: EFAULT reaches the caller's x0 through do_ipc for the
three immediate sites (mini_send, kernel-call request, kernel-call
reply), and a blocked receiver's *parked* x0 for the deferred flush --
p.regs.x[0] = e as i64 as u64, the MINIX retreg idiom
do_exit::unblock_dependents already uses -- replacing a `let _ =` that
dropped the error. That path also sets and clears MF_MSGFAILED, which
has existed unused since Phase 2.

ipc/message.rs ends with zero unsafe: messages stage through a [u8; 104]
and are reassembled by infallible indexing, so every raw-pointer
operation in the user-copy path is in mm::uaccess alone. offset_of!
asserts tie its M_TYPE_OFF / PAYLOAD_OFF to the real Message layout --
without them a field added ahead of payload would be a silent miscopy,
since the slice length would still be correct.

The page-split arithmetic (page_chunks / PageChunk / USER_PAGE_SIZE) is
in kernel-shared beside user_va_ok, because the kernel crate has no
#[cfg(test)] and this is the one piece with real off-by-one risk.
kernel-shared goes 60 -> 68 tests. Granule coupling that was previously
convention is now pinned: USER_PAGE_SIZE == FRAME_SIZE in uaccess.rs
(chunker and walker live in different crates), FRAME_SIZE == PAGE_SIZE
and 1 << PAGE_SHIFT == PAGE_SIZE in addrspace.rs.

D2 -- SYS_DIAGCTL. Servers run at EL0 with no console; every bring-up bug
so far has been diagnosed indirectly through kernel traces. The call
takes a MINIX-numbered subcode (DIAGCTL_CODE_DIAG = 1, 2-4 reserved and
EINVAL) and carries its text *inline* in the payload -- length in 4..8,
up to DIAG_TEXT_MAX = 88 bytes from DIAG_TEXT_OFF = 8. Inline rather than
MINIX 3's (buf, len) user pointer precisely so the debug channel needs no
user-copy machinery and cannot fault: it has to work while the copy
engine and grants are themselves under construction.

The [diag <name>] prefix is the caller's kernel-known Proc::name, never
payload data, so a server can only identify itself -- the anti-spoof
property DS already relies on for m_source. Text is sanitized to
printable ASCII, which is what guarantees one call is exactly one line
and keeps the grep -aF marker contract intact. No new privilege wiring:
k_call_mask already restricts kernel calls to server-grade privs and the
shared USER priv has an empty mask.

server-rt::diag_print is the client, chunking longer strings. It is
called from sef_startup (before init_fresh, so the line proves
SYS_DIAGCTL independently of DS), so all six SEF servers announce
themselves for one line of code.

Proof. Four one-shot probes on stub A's prologue cover every arm of the
engine: an unmapped page, a page-straddling buffer (8 bytes in A's stack
page, 96 in the unmapped page above), the deferred-flush path, and a
mapped-but-read-only destination for the writable check. The last was
added on review -- without it a regression dropping that check would
still have passed every marker; it is mutation-tested, stubbing the check
out makes exactly that marker disappear. A fifth stub was rejected:
NR_STUB_PROCS feeds FORK_POOL_BASE, so it would shift init's forked
children 15 -> 16 and break three existing markers.

Boot markers go 26 -> 31, all unsampled so they cannot drift with IPC
ordering (the [ipc N] form embeds a running counter). qemu-boot.forbidden
gains the same-EL banner "!!! kernel exception (vector index", the sharp
canary for exactly the regression this slice prevents.

The highest risk here was *surfacing* a previously-silent failure: the
kernel-originated notifies (deliver_alarm, deliver_ksig, mini_pf_send,
send_no_quantum) set MF_DELIVERMSG on a proc whose deliver_msg_vir came
from its own last RECEIVE, and the old `let _ =` swallowed a bad one. The
guard is a stub-free boot grepped for [efault], which must be empty. It
is, across both feature configurations.

Drive-bys, per the slice scope and slice 5.0's nominations:
NR_KERN_CALLS_PHASE4 -> NR_KERN_CALLS (25 references; the C header always
emitted the un-suffixed name and the two must not diverge past the 5.6
ABI freeze -- a test now forbids any phase-scoped name in the header);
sef.receive(..) != 0 -> != OK, which was 5 sites, not the 9 slice 5.0
estimated, since drivers/, fs/ and userland/ have no receive loops yet;
ipc_const.rs's trap-ABI comment said x16 where the register is x1; and
the stale slice-2.5-era module docs in ipc/{message,senda,mod}.rs plus
arch/aarch64/userland.rs, which still promised this slice's own work as
future slice-3.4 work.
